requirements.requirement: Both /tmp and /dev/shm ignore program execution, setuid bits, and device nodes.
requirements.summary: Both filesystems were directly observed with nosuid,nodev,noexec. Post-reboot functional probes showed execution and device-node access blocked on each mount; controlled nosuid probes returned the caller UID, and the temporarily changed exec option was restored.

requirements.requirement: The hardened mount settings survive a reboot.
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, the reboot was acknowledged, connectivity was disrupted, and node1 returned with a different boot ID. It was running normally with both persistent fstab entries, hardened live mounts, correct permissions, and working ordinary I/O; subsequent behavioral probes also passed.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Both mounts enforce nosuid,nodev,noexec behavior, and a directly observed reboot demonstrated persistence and healthy recovery. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for the sole managed node and is independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The fstab update, live mount changes, and reboot directly supported the task. Temporary execution, setuid, device-node, and I/O probes were bounded and removed; temporary exec remounts used for nosuid testing were restored to noexec. The retained pre-change fstab backup was a reasonable recovery safeguard. Final lifecycle observations show no failed services, package damage, new exposure, or executor probe residue.
